predictions.directions: intrinsic N1, N2 (analytic, normalised); the fold's 8 null, 3 published, 8 contrast unit directions (delta/||delta|| at 1.0 kcal/mol, re-checked on read: |M v| <= 1e-9 for null/published, contrast orthogonal to the null bases and inside int22/int21/int11/bulge); exploratory: 8 random unit directions on the coverage columns, SeedSequence([20261012, 10, j])
predictions.estimate: all 11,970 TR0+TS0 sequences, K = 2000 pbacktrack samples each (md.uniq_ML = 1), 8 workers; per-sequence sample variances (ddof 1); intervals by bootstrap over sequences, 2000 draws
predictions.exploratory_user: Spearman correlation between I(v) and the fold's genuine changed-MFE fraction at matched norm (1 and 16 kcal/mol), across all 19 fold directions AND within the null group (8 random + 3 published = 11); the across-19 value mostly measures the gap between the groups
predictions.must_hold: c(s).N1 = c(s).N2 = 0 exactly (integers) for every sampled structure; exact reconstruction c(s).theta_0 + o(s) = eval_structure on a subsample (the first sample of every 4th sequence per shard)
predictions.question_user: how much information does likelihood training on TR0+TS0 carry about each direction class?
predictions.registered_test_user: the contrast/null ratio of mean I (8 contrast vs 8 random null directions) exceeds 1: bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 1. No magnitude predicted. THE ONLY REGISTERED TEST.
predictions.report_user: every I(v) also as the Cramer-Rao standard error 1/sqrt(I(v)) in kcal/mol
predictions.reported_check_not_a_prediction_user: I(v) > 0 for every random null direction (bootstrap lower bound). It cannot fail: a sum of variances is positive for any direction some competing structure uses. Reported beside the exact zero for N1 and N2, because 'Type A exactly 0, Type B above 0' is the taxonomy's central point.
predictions.scope_user: E1 measures likelihood training only. Margin training, which is MXfold2's loss, sees competing structures only through the highest-scoring one, and E1 does not measure it.
predictions.spectrum_user: eigenvalues of N_nt^T F N_nt (426 x 426); split-half noise floor = largest |eigenvalue| of (F_A - F_B)/2, halves = first and second K/2 samples; report how many eigenvalues fall below 1% of the median contrast information, and how many below the noise floor
predictions.theory_user: for P(s|x) proportional to exp(-c(s).theta/kT), the Hessian of -log P(ref|x) is Cov_P[c(s)]/(kT)^2, independent of the reference; I(v) = sum over sequences of Var_{s~P(.|x)}[c(s).v]/(kT)^2 at Turner 2004, d0, special_hp 0, 37 C
